title: Classic Savings Account: balance rules, interest and benefits
text: The Classic Savings Account is Saffronleaf Bank's standard savings account for individuals aged 18 and above. The minimum balance is measured as an average monthly balance (AMB), which is the sum of your end-of-day balances for each day of the month divided by the number of days in that month. The required AMB depends on the category of your home branch: ₹10,000 for metro and urban branches, ₹5,000 for semi-urban branches and ₹2,500 for rural branches. Metro and urban branches include those in Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Pune and Ahmedabad. If you transfer your account to a branch in a different category, the new AMB applies from the first day of the following month. If the AMB is not maintained, a non-maintenance charge of 6% of the shortfall is levied, capped at ₹400 per month plus GST. The charge is never allowed to take your balance below zero. Interest on Classic Savings is 3.00% per annum on balances up to ₹1 lakh and 3.50% per annum on the portion above ₹1 lakh. Interest is calculated on the daily closing balance and credited once a year, on 31 March, for all Saffronleaf savings accounts. It is not credited quarterly. Every Classic account comes with a RuPay Classic debit card and one free cheque book of 25 leaves each financial year. To open the account you need your PAN card or Form 60, Aadhaar or another officially valid address proof, and a recent photograph.

title: Prime Savings Account: balance rules, interest and benefits
text: The Prime Savings Account is Saffronleaf Bank's premium savings account. Unlike the Classic account, Prime is measured on an average quarterly balance, not a monthly one. You must maintain an average quarterly balance of ₹25,000 at every branch, whatever the branch category. The average quarterly balance is the sum of your end-of-day balances for every day of the quarter divided by the number of days in the quarter. Quarters end on 30 June, 30 September, 31 December and 31 March. If the average quarterly balance is not maintained, a flat charge of ₹600 per quarter plus GST is levied. If the shortfall continues for two consecutive quarters, the account is converted to Classic Savings at the start of the next quarter, and the Classic balance rules and debit card then apply. Interest on Prime Savings is 3.25% per annum on balances up to ₹5 lakh, and balances above ₹5 lakh earn 4.00% per annum on the portion above ₹5 lakh. Interest is calculated on the daily closing balance and credited once a year, on 31 March. Prime account holders receive a Visa Platinum debit card, and its annual fee is waived for Prime Savings account holders. Other benefits: unlimited free transactions at Saffronleaf ATMs, two free cheque books of 25 leaves each financial year, free demand drafts up to ₹50,000 per day, and a 25% discount on locker rent at participating branches. The account can be opened by individuals aged 18 and above with the same documents as Classic Savings.

title: Debit card variants, limits and replacement
text: Saffronleaf Bank issues two debit cards. RuPay Classic debit card: issued free with Classic Savings, with an annual fee of ₹150 plus GST from the second year. Daily limits are ₹25,000 for ATM cash withdrawal and ₹50,000 for purchases at shops and online combined. Visa Platinum debit card: issued with Prime Savings and available to Classic customers on request. Annual fee ₹499 plus GST, charged in the card's anniversary month; the fee is waived for Prime Savings account holders. Daily limits are ₹75,000 for ATM cash withdrawal and ₹2,00,000 for purchases. Both cards are contactless, and tap payments up to ₹5,000 do not need a PIN. You can lower your daily limits in the mobile app at any time; increases above the standard limits are not possible. Lost, stolen or damaged cards: block the card first, as described on the fraud reporting page. A replacement card costs ₹200 plus GST for RuPay Classic and ₹300 plus GST for Visa Platinum. Replacement cards are produced centrally and sent by registered post to your registered address, and delivery takes up to 15 working days. We do not offer express delivery or instant cards at branches. While you wait, you can keep using UPI, net banking and cardless cash withdrawal at Saffronleaf ATMs. A new card arrives inactive; set its PIN at any Saffronleaf ATM or in the app. The card PIN is separate from your UPI PIN.

title: ATM free transactions, charges and failed withdrawals
text: Free ATM transactions each calendar month depend on your account. Classic Savings: 5 transactions at Saffronleaf ATMs, plus 3 at other banks' ATMs in the six metro centres (Mumbai, New Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru and Hyderabad) or 5 at other banks' ATMs elsewhere. Prime Savings: unlimited at Saffronleaf ATMs and 5 at other banks' ATMs anywhere. Both cash withdrawals and balance enquiries count as transactions. Beyond the free limit, each cash withdrawal costs ₹23 plus GST and each non-financial transaction, such as a balance enquiry or mini statement, costs ₹11 plus GST. Withdrawals declined because of insufficient balance cost ₹25 plus GST. Failed ATM withdrawals: if your account is debited but no cash is dispensed, the amount is automatically reversed within 5 working days of the transaction. You don't need to raise a complaint for this to happen. If the reversal takes longer than 5 working days, Saffronleaf Bank credits compensation of ₹100 for every day of delay, without you having to ask. Keep the ATM slip or the SMS alert, and if the money hasn't come back by the sixth working day, report it in the app under Help, ATM issue, or call the helpline. Cardless cash withdrawal is available at all Saffronleaf ATMs up to ₹10,000 per day using a code generated in the app.

title: Using your debit card abroad: activation and foreign currency charges
text: International usage on all Saffronleaf debit cards is switched off by default. This covers payments at shops and ATMs outside India and online payments to merchants based abroad. You can enable it in the mobile app under Cards, Manage usage, through net banking, or at your branch. Important: for security reasons, an international usage request becomes active only 48 hours after you submit it. We cannot speed this up, including through the helpline, so please enable it at least 48 hours before you travel. When enabling, you choose the countries, or all countries, and an end date of up to 180 days; usage switches off automatically after the end date. Charges: every transaction in a foreign currency attracts a foreign currency markup of 3.5% on the RuPay Classic card and 2% on the Visa Platinum card, plus GST on the markup. The markup also applies to online payments in rupees to merchants registered abroad. ATM withdrawals abroad cost ₹150 plus GST each, in addition to the markup and any fee charged by the ATM owner. Balance enquiries abroad cost ₹25 plus GST. International daily limits are the same as your domestic limits. If a card payment abroad is declined, first check that international usage is active for that country and that the 48 hours have passed. When a terminal abroad offers to charge you in rupees, choose the local currency instead to avoid the merchant's conversion rate.

title: UPI and IMPS limits, effective 1 April 2024
text: UPI and IMPS limits, effective 1 April 2024. UPI: you can send up to ₹1,00,000 per day across up to 10 UPI transactions per day from each Saffronleaf account. A single UPI payment can be up to ₹1,00,000. For UPI payments to verified merchants for tax, hospital and education payments, the limit is ₹5,00,000 per transaction. New device or new registration: when you register UPI on a new phone, or re-register on the same phone after changing your SIM, transfers are capped at ₹5,000 for the first 24 hours. Collect requests, where someone requests money from you, are limited to ₹2,000 each. IMPS: through net banking and the mobile app, you can send up to ₹2,00,000 per day. At branches, IMPS has no upper limit but needs a signed form. Charges: UPI is free. IMPS through the app is free up to ₹1,000; above that it costs ₹5 plus GST per transfer. NEFT and RTGS through digital channels are free. Failed UPI payments where your account is debited are reversed automatically within 1 working day; if not, raise a complaint in the app under Help, UPI issue.

title: UPI and IMPS limits, effective 1 August 2026 (replaces the April 2024 version)
text: UPI and IMPS limits, effective 1 August 2026. This version replaces the limits effective 1 April 2024. UPI: you can send up to ₹1,00,000 per day across up to 20 UPI transactions per day from each Saffronleaf account. A single UPI payment can be up to ₹1,00,000. For UPI payments to verified merchants for tax, hospital and education payments, the limit is ₹5,00,000 per transaction. New device or new registration: when you register UPI on a new phone, or re-register on the same phone after changing your SIM, transfers are capped at ₹5,000 for the first 72 hours, after which the normal daily limit applies automatically. This cooling period cannot be lifted by the helpline or a branch. Collect requests are limited to ₹2,000 each, and collect requests from numbers not in your contacts are blocked by default. IMPS: through net banking and the mobile app, you can send up to ₹5,00,000 per day. At branches, IMPS has no upper limit but needs a signed form. Charges: UPI is free. IMPS through the app is now free for all amounts. NEFT and RTGS through digital channels remain free. What changed in this version: the daily UPI transaction count rose from 10 to 20, the new device cap now lasts 72 hours instead of 24 hours, the IMPS daily limit rose to ₹5,00,000, and IMPS charges in the app were removed. Failed UPI payments where your account is debited are reversed automatically within 1 working day.

title: Fixed deposits: rates, premature withdrawal and renewal
text: Saffronleaf Bank fixed deposits can be opened for any period from 7 days to 10 years with a minimum of ₹5,000. Current interest rates for deposits below ₹3 crore, effective 1 September 2026: 7 to 45 days 3.50%; 46 to 179 days 5.25%; 180 days to less than 1 year 6.25%; 1 year 6.80%; above 1 year up to 3 years 7.00%; above 3 years up to 10 years 6.50%. Senior citizens aged 60 and above get an extra 0.50% on all tenures, so the 1 year rate for senior citizens is 7.30%. Interest can be paid out monthly or quarterly, or reinvested and paid at maturity. Premature withdrawal: a fixed deposit closed before 180 days earns no interest at all; only the principal is returned. For deposits closed after 180 days, interest is paid at the rate applicable for the period the deposit actually ran, minus a penalty of 1%. Tax-saver deposits have a 5-year lock-in and cannot be closed early. Partial withdrawals are not allowed; you must close the whole deposit. Premature closure can be done in the app for deposits opened online, or at your branch. Auto-renewal: unless you instruct otherwise, deposits renew on maturity for the same tenure at the rate then in force. Tax is deducted at source on interest as per income tax rules; submit Form 15G or 15H at the start of each financial year if eligible. Instead of breaking a deposit, you can take a loan or overdraft of up to 90% of the deposit amount.

title: Cheque books, stop payment and Positive Pay
text: Cheque books: Classic Savings includes one free cheque book of 25 leaves each financial year and Prime Savings includes two. Additional cheque books cost ₹4 per leaf plus GST. Request one in the app, through net banking, at an ATM or at the branch; it is delivered by courier to your registered address within 7 working days. Stop payment: you can stop payment of a cheque you have issued, as long as it has not yet been paid. The charge is ₹100 per cheque, or ₹300 for a range of consecutive cheques, plus GST. Requests made through the app or net banking take effect immediately; requests at the branch take effect once processed, usually within 2 hours. A stop payment remains in force until you revoke it in writing. Positive Pay: for cheques of ₹50,000 and above, we recommend submitting the cheque details (date, payee name, amount and cheque number) in the app before handing over the cheque. For cheques of ₹5 lakh and above, Positive Pay confirmation is mandatory, and cheques without it will be returned. Cheque return charges: a cheque you issued that bounces for insufficient funds costs ₹500 plus GST per instance; a cheque you deposited that is returned unpaid costs ₹150 plus GST. Clearing: cheques deposited before 2:00 pm on a working day are usually credited the next working day.

title: Personal loans: rates, prepayment and foreclosure
text: Saffronleaf personal loans range from ₹50,000 to ₹15 lakh for tenures of 12 to 60 months, at fixed interest rates of 11.25% to 19.50% per annum depending on your credit profile. The processing fee is 2% of the loan amount, minimum ₹2,500, plus GST. EMIs are debited on the 5th of each month from your Saffronleaf account. Prepayment rules: part-prepayment is not allowed on personal loans, so you cannot pay a lump sum to reduce your EMI or tenure. You can foreclose, meaning repay the entire outstanding loan, only after 12 EMIs have been paid. A foreclosure charge of 4% of the outstanding principal plus GST applies. To foreclose, request a foreclosure statement in the app or at your branch; it is valid for 7 days, and the loan is closed once the amount is paid. A no-dues certificate is issued within 10 working days. Late payment: a bounced EMI costs ₹550 plus GST, and overdue amounts attract a penal charge of 2% per month. Home loans work differently: floating-rate home loans taken by individuals have no prepayment or foreclosure charges, and part-prepayments of any amount are accepted. Fixed-rate home loans carry a 2% prepayment charge. Applying for any loan involves a credit bureau check, and a minimum credit score of 700 is usually required for personal loans.

title: Reporting fraud, lost cards and unauthorised transactions
text: If you notice a transaction you did not make, or your card, phone or cheque book is lost or stolen, act immediately. Block your card instantly in the mobile app under Cards, Block card, or call the 24-hour fraud helpline on 1800 419 2020, toll-free within India, or +91 22 4419 2020 from abroad. You can also send an SMS saying BLOCK followed by the last 4 digits of your card to 98200 41920 from your registered mobile number. Your liability for unauthorised electronic transactions depends on how quickly you tell us: reported within 3 working days of receiving our alert, zero liability; within 4 to 7 working days, your liability is limited to ₹10,000 for savings accounts; after 7 working days, it is decided under the bank's board-approved policy. Unauthorised amounts are shadow-credited to your account within 10 working days of your report, and complaints are resolved within 90 days. Saffronleaf staff will never ask for your OTP, card PIN, CVV, UPI PIN or net banking password, whether by phone, SMS, email or social media, and we never ask you to install screen-sharing apps. If anyone does, it is a fraud attempt: hang up and report it to us. You can also report cyber fraud on the national cyber crime reporting portal.

title: Branch hours, cash counters and branch services
text: Saffronleaf branches are open Monday to Friday from 9:30 am to 4:30 pm. The cash counter closes earlier, at 3:30 pm, on weekdays; after that, branches handle only non-cash services such as account opening, KYC updates, cheque book requests and demand draft collection. On the 1st, 3rd and 5th Saturdays of the month branches are open from 9:30 am to 1:30 pm, and the cash counter on those Saturdays closes at 12:30 pm. Branches are closed on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays, on Sundays and on public holidays. Cash deposits of ₹50,000 or more in a single transaction need your PAN card or Form 60. In Classic Savings, the first 4 cash deposits at the branch each month are free; from the 5th deposit, each costs ₹50 plus GST. Cash deposit machines at 600 locations accept deposits 24 hours a day, up to ₹49,900 per transaction using your debit card. Demand drafts cost ₹50 for amounts up to ₹10,000, and ₹3 per ₹1,000 above that, with a maximum charge of ₹10,000. Coins and soiled notes are exchanged free of charge at all branches during cash counter hours. Senior citizens and persons with disabilities can request doorstep banking for cash pickup and delivery at ₹100 plus GST per visit.

title: Periodic KYC update and what happens if it is overdue
text: Every Saffronleaf customer must periodically update their KYC (Know Your Customer) records. The interval depends on your risk category: every 2 years for high-risk customers, every 8 years for medium-risk customers and every 10 years for low-risk customers. We remind you by SMS and email at least 60 days before the due date. If there is no change in your details, you can update KYC through a self-declaration in the app, through net banking, by email from your registered email address, or at any branch; no documents are needed. If your address has changed, upload the new address proof in the app or submit it at a branch; address changes are verified within 7 working days. If your identity document has expired or your name has changed, you will need to complete video KYC or visit a branch. If you miss the due date, there is a 30-day grace period, after which debits on the account are blocked. Credits such as salary and interest continue to come in, but withdrawals, transfers, card payments and UPI payments will fail. Full access is restored within 2 working days of completing the update. Accounts with KYC pending for more than 12 months may be frozen completely. Video KYC is available from 9 am to 9 pm on all days except national holidays.

title: Closing an account and inoperative accounts
text: Closing your account: accounts can be closed at your home branch or any branch in the same city by submitting a signed closure form along with unused cheque leaves and your debit card. Closure within 14 days of opening is free; closure after 14 days but within 12 months of opening costs ₹500 plus GST; closure after 12 months is free. The balance is paid by transfer to another account in your name; cash payout is limited to ₹20,000. Standing instructions, loan EMIs and investments linked to the account must be moved before closure. Inoperative accounts: if there are no customer-initiated transactions for 2 years, the account is classified as inoperative. Interest continues to be credited. The debit card, UPI and net banking stop working, and outgoing transactions are not allowed until the account is reactivated. To reactivate, submit a request with fresh KYC at any branch or through video KYC; there is no charge, and reactivation is completed within 3 working days. Balances in accounts that stay inoperative for 10 years are transferred to the regulator's depositor education fund, but you can claim the money back at any time through the bank. Minimum balance charges are not applied on inoperative accounts.
